source_title: Opposition Meets at Kharge's Residence, Plans Public Impeachment of CEC - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Leaders from the INDIA bloc gathered at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi for a strategy meeting to plan a public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The venue was relocated to Kharge's official residence after permissions were reportedly denied for earlier locations, including Hotel Ashoka. The planned public proceedings are structured to reflect parliamentary functioning, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar expected to preside over the session. The meeting was attended by senior opposition figures, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Derek O'Brien, Jairam Ramesh, and John Brittas. Leaders highlighted that representatives from opposition parties and civil society will participate, with motions to be moved and discussed by the Leaders of Opposition from both Houses. The opposition continues to target the Election Commission over electoral integrity concerns ahead of a planned mega rally. Read More

Rahul Gandhi Urges People To Join Chalo Dilli March At Ramlila Maidan
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has issued a call for the Chalo Dilli protest march scheduled for 1st November at Ramlila Maidan. Describing it as a march for the soul of the country and a Save Democracy initiative, he urged citizens, opposition workers, and student groups across political lines to participate. Addressing the public, he asserted that people should not worry about police lathis and stated that the march aims to protect the Constitution and protest against alleged vote theft. India Today correspondent Moushumi Singh reported that the rally represents an attempt by the India Bloc to build momentum and mobilise public support ahead of a public impeachment planned at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. The demonstration is expected to see participation from civil society and opposition party workers arriving from neighbouring states including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Haryana.
Rahul Gandhi: 'Election Commission Is Not Functioning As The Election Commission Of India'
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticised the Election Commission, alleging it is not functioning as the Election Commission of India and is not doing its job. He claimed to have 'concrete 100% proof of Election Commission allowing cheating in a seat in Karnataka', asserting this pattern is occurring across constituency after constituency. Gandhi alleged irregularities in voter addition and deletion, claiming thousands of new voters aged 45 to 65 were added in a single constituency.
Row Over SIR: Karnataka Minister Backs Voter Deletions, Rahul Gandhi Opposes, BJP Mocks
A major political controversy has emerged as Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka, differing from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's nationwide stance. Jarkiholi maintained that the enumeration and deletion of nearly one crore voters in Karnataka was properly conducted, removing duplicate, relocated, and deceased electors. He stated that the party's objections were focused on states such as West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Bihar. In contrast, Rahul Gandhi has fiercely attacked the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the drive, alleging vote rigging and the disenfranchisement of genuine voters while demanding the exercise be halted. The divergence has triggered attacks from the Bharatiya Janata Party, which claimed Congress leaders are exposing Rahul Gandhi's claims. Meanwhile, other Congress leaders have questioned the Karnataka deletions, citing reports of living electors being erroneously marked as dead and reaffirming full backing for Rahul Gandhi's nationwide campaign.
BJP Mocks Congress Over Ballot Paper Defeat in MLC Polls Amid 'Vote Chori' Row
The Bharatiya Janata Party has launched a sharp attack against the Congress following the outcome of the Legislative Council elections across four states, where polling was conducted using ballot papers. Highlighting that the Congress secured only one seat while the BJP won 16 out of 28 seats, the party questioned the opposition's ongoing 'vote chori' campaign against electronic voting machines. Party leaders stated that the Congress has consistently demanded a return to paper ballots, yet failed to secure voter backing when ballot papers were actually deployed. Union Minister and BJP President JP Nadda criticised the opposition's conduct, saying political credibility must be established with verifiable facts before approaching the Election Commission instead of raising unproven allegations over voter rolls. In response, Congress leaders such as Pawan Khera challenged the government to conduct the upcoming assembly elections using ballot papers if the BJP is truly confident.

इंडिया गठबंधन के नेताओं ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ 'सार्वजनिक महाभियोग' की योजना बनाने के लिए कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे के नई दिल्ली स्थित आवास पर एक रणनीति बैठक की। होटल अशोक सहित अन्य स्थानों पर अनुमति न मिलने के बाद बैठक का आयोजन खड़गे के आधिकारिक आवास पर किया गया।

## प्रस्तावित कार्यवाही
यह प्रस्तावित सार्वजनिक सत्र संसदीय कामकाज की तर्ज पर आयोजित किया जाएगा, जिसकी अध्यक्षता पूर्व लोकसभा अध्यक्ष मीरा कुमार द्वारा किए जाने की संभावना है। सत्र की मुख्य बातें इस प्रकार हैं:
* विपक्षी दलों के प्रतिनिधियों और नागरिक समाज के सदस्यों की भागीदारी।
* संसद के दोनों सदनों में विपक्ष के नेताओं द्वारा प्रस्ताव पेश करना और उन पर चर्चा करना।

## व्यापक संदर्भ और विरोध प्रदर्शन
यह पहल कांग्रेस नेता राहुल गांधी द्वारा 1 नवंबर को रामलीला मैदान में 'चलो दिल्ली' मार्च के आह्वान के बाद आई है। राहुल गांधी ने मतदाता सूची में कथित गड़बड़ियों का आरोप लगाते हुए चुनाव आयोग पर निशाना साधा है और लोगों से संविधान की रक्षा के लिए इस मार्च में शामिल होने का आग्रह किया है।

इस बीच, मतदाता सूची के विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) को लेकर राजनीतिक बहस तेज हो गई है। जहाँ राहुल गांधी ने इसे धांधली करार देते हुए रोकने की मांग की है, वहीं कर्नाटक के मंत्री सतीश जारकीहोली ने राज्य में इसे एक सामान्य प्रक्रिया बताते हुए इसका बचाव किया है। दूसरी ओर, भारतीय जनता पार्टी ने कांग्रेस की आलोचना करते हुए हालिया विधान परिषद चुनावों में बैलट पेपर के उपयोग के दौरान पार्टी के प्रदर्शन पर सवाल उठाए हैं।

en_body:
Leaders from the INDIA bloc held a strategy meeting at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi to organize a planned public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The meeting venue was shifted to Kharge's residence after requests for other locations, such as Hotel Ashoka, were reportedly declined. 

## Planned Proceedings
The upcoming public session is designed to mirror formal parliamentary operations. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar is expected to preside over the proceedings. Key highlights include:
* Participation from opposition party representatives and civil society members.
* Motions to be moved and debated by the Leaders of Opposition from both houses of Parliament.

## Wider Context and Protests
The initiative follows a call from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for a 'Chalo Dilli' march at Ramlila Maidan, scheduled for November 1. Gandhi, who has alleged irregularities in voter rolls and accused the Election Commission of failure to maintain electoral integrity, urged supporters to join the event to "protect the Constitution."

Meanwhile, a political debate has intensified regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls. While Rahul Gandhi has demanded a halt to the exercise alleging vote rigging, Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi defended the process in his state as a routine removal of duplicate or deceased electors. Concurrently, the Bharatiya Janata Party has criticized the Congress, pointing to the party's recent performance in Legislative Council elections where ballot papers were used, challenging the opposition's ongoing stance against electronic voting machines.
